story: Trap is named after the Atlanta term "trap house", a drug house, and the Atlanta rapper T.I. says he coined the word with his 2003 album Trap Muzik. In the mid-2000s Atlanta producers DJ Toomp, Shawty Redd and Zaytoven set its sound: synth, orchestra and string swells over 808 kick drums. Lex Luger, born in 1991, drummed in church bands, made beats on an unlicensed copy of FL Studio and from late 2008 posted them on Myspace. In 2009 the rapper Waka Flocka Flame wrote back, and later flew him to Atlanta. Luger produced most of Waka's album Flockaveli (5 October 2010): 808 trills, bass kicks, hand claps, dense synthesizers and shifting sub-bass layers under constant ad-libs. He produced more than 200 songs in 2010 and 2011, and other producers copied his sounds. Beats often run in half-time, around 70 BPM, for finer hi-hat subdivisions. The trio Migos, formed in Lawrenceville, Georgia, in 2008, broke out in 2013 with "Versace", produced by Zaytoven. In Chicago, Chief Keef's "I Don't Like" and "Love Sosa" spawned drill as a subgenre of trap. Katy Perry's "Dark Horse" with Juicy J reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in January 2014.

disagreements: Start date: our record says 2010; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music?action=raw gives "cultural_origins  = 1990s, [[Atlanta]]" and "the modern sound of trap emerged in 1999". 2010 fits the record's 'modern trap' as the Lex Luger / Flockaveli sound ("The style was popularized by [[Record producer|producer]] [[Lex Luger (record producer)|Lex Luger]], who produced the influential [[Waka Flocka Flame]] album ''[[Flockaveli]]'' in 2010"), so this is a scope difference, not an error.
notes: No home-language article applies (English). The 'Migos flow' triplet marker in our record could not be sourced from the pages read: the trap article only lists a journal paper titled 'Triplet Flow in Recent Hip-Hop Music' in its bibliography, so the story names Migos and 'Versace' without describing their flow. T.I.'s coining of the term is his own claim and is attributed. Lex Luger's Virginia origin was left out: the page names his crew 'Virginia Boyz Productionz' and a high school but does not say where he grew up.
